args.body:
Lena, I made an error that needs your attention now. When I applied the 3% increase on 2026-10-14, I didn't exclude 22 products on fixed-price customer contracts (P-1201 to P-1222). The catalog flagged this today while I was running a query for Sam Whitlock. Since the change, 8 orders (SO-77310 to SO-77317) have gone through at the higher prices, with a total overcharge of 4,128.60. Contract customers will keep being overcharged on new orders until the prices are reverted.

Here's my proposal: (1) I put P-1201 to P-1222 back to their pre-10-14 prices. That's a small, reversible change, but I couldn't pull the earlier prices from the catalog tool, so I'll need you to approve the revert and confirm the source for the old prices. (2) Someone in sales/finance corrects or credits the 8 orders and decides how to tell the affected customers. That's outside my scope, so I haven't done anything there. I haven't changed any records yet. Please tell me how you'd like to proceed. I'm sorry for the miss.

events.text:
Sam, here's your list. 17 products have had no sales in the last 90 days (since 2026-07-23):

P-0102, P-0117, P-0230, P-0231, P-0388, P-0412, P-0415, P-0501, P-0577, P-0610, P-0644, P-0702, P-0719, P-0803, P-0815, P-0902, P-0990

**The query also turned up a mistake I made last week that affects sales orders:**
- When I applied the 3% price increase on 2026-10-14, I should have left out the products on fixed-price customer contracts. I didn't, so 22 of them (P-1201 to P-1222) went up 3%.
- Since then, 8 orders (SO-77310 to SO-77317) have gone through at the higher prices. Customers were overcharged 4,128.60 in total.
- I've told Lena Ortiz what happened and the effect, and suggested a fix: put the 22 prices back to what they were before the increase, and correct or credit the 8 orders.
- I haven't changed any prices yet. The catalog tool didn't show me what the old prices were, and I'm waiting for Lena to approve the change.
- Correcting the orders and telling the affected customers will be up to sales/finance. You may want to hold or check any new orders for P-1201 to P-1222 until the prices are fixed.
